scenes.tts: Why does far less of the energy captured by Bay plankton reach the osprey level? Watch a gold band of energy cross the Chesapeake Bay. It enters green phytoplankton from sunlight. Then teal zooplankton, menhaden, and an osprey take turns feeding. The band will change at every step.
scenes.caption: Why does far less of the energy captured by Bay plankton reach the osprey level? Watch a gold band of energy cross the Chesapeake Bay. It enters green phytoplankton from sunlight. Then teal zooplankton, menhaden, and an osprey take turns feeding. The band will change at every step.
scenes.visual: Hook first. Fill the frame with one Chesapeake Bay cross-section: sun upper left, water through the middle, plankton magnified below, menhaden swimming right, osprey above. COLOR MAP for both films: energy GOLD, living carbon and producer tissue GREEN, consumers TEAL, decomposers BLUE, heat RED. A thick GOLD band moves from sun toward phytoplankton, then pauses under question marks between organisms. Keep water drifting and fish swimming slowly. No title yet.
scenes.narration: Why does far less of the energy captured by Bay plankton reach the osprey level? Watch a gold band of energy cross the Chesapeake Bay. It enters green phytoplankton from sunlight. Then teal zooplankton, menhaden, and an osprey take turns feeding. The band will change at every step.

scenes.visual: Keep the moving Bay dimly visible. Show the title 'Why Energy Pyramids Narrow' for two seconds, then transform the title into a small corner label.

scenes.tts: Phytoplankton are producers because they capture light energy and store it in food. Animals are consumers because they get energy by eating. Blue decomposers get energy from dead matter and wastes. Gold arrows point from food to eater. Those arrows follow energy, not the animal doing the hunting.
scenes.caption: Phytoplankton are producers because they capture light energy and store it in food. Animals are consumers because they get energy by eating. Blue decomposers get energy from dead matter and wastes. Gold arrows point from food to eater. Those arrows follow energy, not the animal doing the hunting.
scenes.visual: Use the same cross-section. GREEN phytoplankton enlarge and gain a 'producer' label. TEAL zooplankton, menhaden, and osprey gain one shared 'consumers' brace. BLUE decomposers pulse around dead matter on the bottom. GOLD arrows grow from phytoplankton to zooplankton, zooplankton to menhaden, and menhaden to osprey. Animate arrowheads moving toward each eater.
scenes.narration: Phytoplankton are producers because they capture light energy and store it in food. Animals are consumers because they get energy by eating. Blue decomposers get energy from dead matter and wastes. Gold arrows point from food to eater. Those arrows follow energy, not the animal doing the hunting.

scenes.tts: When zooplankton feed, the incoming gold band splits. Cellular respiration releases part as spreading red heat. Uneaten pieces and undigested waste move toward blue decomposers. Only the tissue branch becomes new zooplankton tissue. That branch is available to a menhaden that feeds next.
scenes.caption: When zooplankton feed, the incoming gold band splits. Cellular respiration releases part as spreading red heat. Uneaten pieces and undigested waste move toward blue decomposers. Only the tissue branch becomes new zooplankton tissue. That branch is available to a menhaden that feeds next.
scenes.visual: Zoom into one large cartoon zooplankton, still within the Bay. A wide GOLD band of prey approaches. Before it enters, GOLD scraps break off the prey and sink toward BLUE decomposers, labeled 'uneaten'. Inside the body the band splits into RED waves labeled 'heat', a GOLD waste pellet leaving the body toward the decomposers labeled 'undigested', and a narrower GOLD band filling a TEAL body patch labeled 'new tissue'. Mark the widths 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: When zooplankton feed, the incoming gold band splits. Cellular respiration releases part as spreading red heat. Uneaten pieces and undigested waste move toward blue decomposers. Only the tissue branch becomes new zooplankton tissue. That branch is available to a menhaden that feeds next.

scenes.tts: Now follow the same split inside a menhaden. Which outgoing branch can become osprey tissue? Watch all branches form. Choose before the labels appear.
scenes.caption: Now follow the same split inside a menhaden. Which outgoing branch can become osprey tissue? Watch all branches form. Choose before the labels appear.
scenes.visual: Transform the zooplankton outline into a large menhaden outline. Rebuild the same unlabeled branches: scraps falling from the prey before it enters, then RED waves, a waste pellet, and a GOLD tissue band inside the fish. Put the question 'Which branch can feed the osprey?' above them. All branches continue moving gently.
scenes.narration: Now follow the same split inside a menhaden. Which outgoing branch can become osprey tissue? Watch all branches form. Choose before the labels appear.

scenes.visual: Deliberate thinking pause. Hold the question and three moving branches for 4.5 seconds. Let RED heat waves spread, scraps sink, and the tissue branch pulse. Do not reveal the answer.

scenes.tts: The branch stored as new menhaden tissue can feed the osprey. Heat has dispersed into water and air. Uneaten or undigested material can still feed decomposers. It does not become osprey tissue through this link. The gold band reaching the osprey is narrower.
scenes.caption: The branch stored as new menhaden tissue can feed the osprey. Heat has dispersed into water and air. Uneaten or undigested material can still feed decomposers. It does not become osprey tissue through this link. The gold band reaching the osprey is narrower.
scenes.visual: Reveal labels on the existing branches. The 'new tissue' branch brightens and extends into the osprey. RED heat fades outward into water and air. Scraps reach BLUE decomposers. Keep a moving GOLD outline around the narrow branch so viewers can follow it.
scenes.narration: The branch stored as new menhaden tissue can feed the osprey. Heat has dispersed into water and air. Uneaten or undigested material can still feed decomposers. It does not become osprey tissue through this link. The gold band reaching the osprey is narrower.

scenes.tts: Ecologists compare levels with energy transfer efficiency. It is the percentage measured at a level that appears at the next. The measurements must match in kind, area, and time. A familiar percentage appears on screen as a rough model. Real feeding steps can be higher or lower.
scenes.caption: Ecologists compare levels with energy transfer efficiency. It is the percentage measured at a level that appears at the next. The measurements must match in kind, area, and time. A familiar percentage appears on screen as a rough model. Real feeding steps can be higher or lower.
scenes.visual: Carry the GOLD input and output bands into a large comparison frame. Add three locks labeled 'same measure', 'same area', and 'same time'. Once all lock, show '10% model' on screen beside a slider spanning '5%–20%'. Label the entire graphic 'schematic'; do not imply the endpoints are universal limits.
scenes.narration: Ecologists compare levels with energy transfer efficiency. It is the percentage measured at a level that appears at the next. The measurements must match in kind, area, and time. A familiar percentage appears on screen as a rough model. Real feeding steps can be higher or lower.

scenes.tts: Stack those matching measurements, with producers at the bottom. The result is an energy pyramid. Each bar is narrower because only part became new tissue above. The shape tracks energy flow, not the body size of any organism. Many small producers can support fewer large predators.
scenes.caption: Stack those matching measurements, with producers at the bottom. The result is an energy pyramid. Each bar is narrower because only part became new tissue above. The shape tracks energy flow, not the body size of any organism. Many small producers can support fewer large predators.
scenes.visual: Transform the horizontal GOLD bands into four centered bars stacked bottom to top: producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers, top consumers. Compute each width from the lesson's repeated model ratio, but show no worked values. Add 'model' above the pyramid. Tiny organism cartoons drift beside their matching bars without controlling bar width.
scenes.narration: Stack those matching measurements, with producers at the bottom. The result is an energy pyramid. Each bar is narrower because only part became new tissue above. The shape tracks energy flow, not the body size of any organism. Many small producers can support fewer large predators.

scenes.tts: A real food web adds branches. Menhaden eat phytoplankton and zooplankton. Striped bass also eat menhaden. An osprey's trophic level can change with the path you follow. The same accounting still works at every link. Follow arrows from each food to its eater.
scenes.caption: A real food web adds branches. Menhaden eat phytoplankton and zooplankton. Striped bass also eat menhaden. An osprey's trophic level can change with the path you follow. The same accounting still works at every link. Follow arrows from each food to its eater.
scenes.visual: Transform the pyramid back into the Bay. Branch the GOLD arrows: phytoplankton to menhaden, phytoplankton to zooplankton, zooplankton to menhaden, and menhaden to both osprey and striped bass. Trace two possible paths to osprey one after the other. Keep every organism moving gently and show no more than six labeled things.
scenes.narration: A real food web adds branches. Menhaden eat phytoplankton and zooplankton. Striped bass also eat menhaden. An osprey's trophic level can change with the path you follow. The same accounting still works at every link. Follow arrows from each food to its eater.

scenes.tts: Return to the osprey. Its food energy began with producers capturing sunlight. Along the path, heat spread and other material moved toward decomposers. The energy was transformed, not destroyed. But at each feeding step, only the tissue branch became available to the next consumer.
scenes.caption: Return to the osprey. Its food energy began with producers capturing sunlight. Along the path, heat spread and other material moved toward decomposers. The energy was transformed, not destroyed. But at each feeding step, only the tissue branch became available to the next consumer.
scenes.visual: Trace one bright GOLD pulse from sun to producer and through one food path to the osprey. At every organism, animate RED heat waves and scraps toward BLUE decomposers. Leave faint GOLD history trails so the full route remains visible without freezing the frame.
scenes.narration: Return to the osprey. Its food energy began with producers capturing sunlight. Along the path, heat spread and other material moved toward decomposers. The energy was transformed, not destroyed. But at each feeding step, only the tissue branch became available to the next consumer.

scenes.tts: That is why energy pyramids narrow even when the exact percentage changes. Use the rule before any shortcut percentage. At each step, only part becomes tissue the next level can eat.
scenes.caption: That is why energy pyramids narrow even when the exact percentage changes. Use the rule before any shortcut percentage. At each step, only part becomes tissue the next level can eat.
scenes.visual: Let the Bay simplify into three moving branches at one feeding step. Fade everything except the narrow new-tissue branch. Then move that branch to the center as the picture prepares for the end card.

scenes.visual: One-line end card only, centered large: 'At each step, only part becomes tissue the next level can eat.' No subtitle, logo line, or smaller text. A faint GOLD band continues moving behind the words.
